newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian tax revenues 74 pct of target in 9 months.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax revenues 74 pct of target in 9 months.

text.p: Russia's federal budget took in 74 percent of targeted tax revenues, or 138 trillion roubles, in the first nine months of this year, a government press statement said on Thursday.
But it said gross tax revenues over the period exceeded those for all of 1995 by 40 percent and were eight percent of gross domestic product.
The release blamed a crisis with payments and barter operations for the shortfall. It also said some energy and industrial enterprises were not paying taxes.
The net tax shortfall as of October was 53.6 trillion roubles, and the amount of deferred tax payments that became due but were not paid totalled 18.4 trillion roubles.
Tax payers failed to pay 3.65 trillion roubles in fines for payment violations.
Energy enterprises still owe 29.4 trillion roubles in unpaid taxes, it said, while heavy industrial enterprises owe 10.1 trillion.
Russia has said it will step up tax collection to plug the budget deficit while maintaining market economy reforms.
Earlier this week, a government commission said it would begin bankruptcy proceedings against six large companies unless they cleared their back taxes within a week.
